COMMON INTEREST DEVELOPMENT OPEN MEETING ACT — HOA BOARD MEETING REQUIREMENTS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association · September 4, 2026

DECLARATION OF ASSOCIATION AND PURPOSE
This information sheet describes California statutory law under the Common Interest Development Open Meeting Act (Civil Code §§ 4900-4955, part of the Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act) as it applies to meetings of the board of directors of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association. It states facts about when board meetings must be open to members, what notice the association must give, what limited topics may be discussed in a closed executive session, members' rights to attend and speak, and the requirement that board action generally be taken at a properly noticed open meeting. It does not evaluate whether any particular past or planned meeting, notice, or board action of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association complied with these requirements.

GENERAL RULE: BOARD ACTION MUST OCCUR AT A BOARD MEETING
The Davis-Stirling Act's Common Interest Development Open Meeting Act, Civil Code § 4900, states: "This article shall be known and may be cited as the Common Interest Development Open Meeting Act." Its central rule appears in Civil Code § 4910(a): "The board shall not take action on any item of business outside of a board meeting." California law also restricts using a series of electronic transmissions (such as email) as a substitute for a meeting for this purpose, except in a narrow emergency circumstance addressed in a separate clause of this document. This rule applies to the board of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This article shall be known and may be cited as the Common Interest Development Open Meeting Act."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4900 (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4900 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4900.)
  "The board shall not take action on any item of business outside of a board meeting."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4910(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4910(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4910.)
  Known gap: The citations to § 4900 and § 4910(a) are independent, separately-numbered sections of the same article (Article 2, "Board Meeting," of Civil Code §§ 4900-4955); § 4900 is the article's short-title provision and § 4910(a) states the operative no-action-outside-a-meeting rule. This clause does not quote § 4910(b), which separately restricts (with a narrow emergency exception) using a series of electronic transmissions, such as email, as a substitute for a meeting; that restriction is described narratively above but not quoted. This clause does not define what qualifies as a validly convened "board meeting" in every circumstance (for example, ad hoc or informal gatherings of directors), a line California's published guidance and case law address in more granular, fact-specific ways than the statutory text alone. This document does not determine whether any specific decision, communication, or gathering involving the association's board did or did not constitute "action" taken "outside of a board meeting."

NOTICE OF BOARD MEETINGS: TIMING, DELIVERY, AND REQUIRED CONTENT
California law sets minimum notice requirements before a board meeting of a common interest development association. Civil Code § 4920(a) provides the general timing rule: "Except as provided in subdivision (b), the association shall give notice of the time and place of a board meeting at least four days before the meeting." A shorter, two-day minimum applies to a nonemergency meeting held solely in executive session: Civil Code § 4920(b)(2) provides, "If a nonemergency board meeting is held solely in executive session, the association shall give notice of the time and place of the meeting at least two days prior to the meeting." A different, notice-free exception applies to a true emergency meeting: Civil Code § 4923 provides, "An emergency board meeting may be called by the president of the association, or by any two directors other than the president, if there are circumstances that could not have been reasonably foreseen which require immediate attention and possible action by the board, and which of necessity make it impracticable to provide notice as required by Section 4920." As to how notice must be delivered, Civil Code § 4920(c) provides: "Notice of a board meeting shall be given by general delivery pursuant to Section 4045," and as to what notice must contain, Civil Code § 4920(d) provides: "Notice of a board meeting shall contain the agenda for the meeting." These timing, delivery, and content requirements apply to board meetings of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Except as provided in subdivision (b), the association shall give notice of the time and place of a board meeting at least four days before the meeting."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4920(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4920(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4920.)
  "If a nonemergency board meeting is held solely in executive session, the association shall give notice of the time and place of the meeting at least two days prior to the meeting."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4920(b)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4920(b)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4920.)
  "An emergency board meeting may be called by the president of the association, or by any two directors other than the president, if there are circumstances that could not have been reasonably foreseen which require immediate attention and possible action by the board, and which of necessity make it impracticable to provide notice as required by Section 4920."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4923 (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4923 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4923.)
  "Notice of a board meeting shall be given by general delivery pursuant to Section 4045."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4920(c) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4920(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4920.)
  "Notice of a board meeting shall contain the agenda for the meeting."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4920(d) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4920(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4920.)
  Known gap: The citations to § 4920(a), § 4920(b)(2), § 4920(c), and § 4920(d) are all subdivisions of the same statutory section, § 4920, and are treated together because they define one integrated notice regime (default timing, the executive-session-only exception, delivery method, and required content). The citation to § 4923 is to a separate, independently-numbered section defining what qualifies as an emergency meeting exempt from advance notice altogether, cross-referenced from § 4920(b)(1) (not independently quoted here). This clause does not quote or verify Civil Code § 4045, the general-delivery mechanics section cross-referenced by § 4920(c), nor does it quote § 4920(b)(3), which allows an association's own governing documents to require a longer notice period than the statutory minimum if the governing documents specifically say so. This document does not state what notice period, if any, the association's own governing documents require, and does not determine whether any specific notice given by the association's board complied with these timing, delivery, or content requirements.

EXECUTIVE SESSION: PERMITTED TOPICS AND MINUTE-NOTATION REQUIREMENT
California law limits the topics a board may discuss in a closed "executive session" to a specific, enumerated list rather than allowing the board to close a meeting for any reason. Civil Code § 4935(a) provides: "The board may adjourn to, or meet solely in, executive session to consider litigation, matters relating to the formation of contracts with third parties, member discipline, personnel matters, or to meet with a member, upon the member's request, regarding the member's payment of assessments, as specified in Section 5665." Even though executive session excludes the general membership, California law requires that what happened there not disappear from the record entirely: Civil Code § 4935(e) provides, "Any matter discussed in executive session shall be generally noted in the minutes of the immediately following meeting that is open to the entire membership." These executive-session limits and the minute-notation requirement apply to the board of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The board may adjourn to, or meet solely in, executive session to consider litigation, matters relating to the formation of contracts with third parties, member discipline, personnel matters, or to meet with a member, upon the member’s request, regarding the member’s payment of assessments, as specified in Section 5665."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4935(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4935(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4935.)
  "Any matter discussed in executive session shall be generally noted in the minutes of the immediately following meeting that is open to the entire membership."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4935(e) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4935(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4935.)
  Known gap: The citations to § 4935(a) and § 4935(e) are subdivisions of the same statutory section. This clause does not separately quote § 4935(b), (c), or (d), which respectively make executive session mandatory (rather than merely permitted) to discuss member discipline if the affected member requests it, to discuss an assessment payment plan under Section 5665, and to decide whether to foreclose a lien under subdivision (b) of Section 5705 -- each identifies additional specific circumstances triggering, or narrowing, the executive-session mechanism beyond the general list in subdivision (a). This document does not determine whether any specific topic actually discussed by the association's board in a closed session fell within this statutory list.

MEMBERS' RIGHT TO ATTEND OPEN MEETINGS AND TO SPEAK
California law gives every member of a common interest development association a right to attend the association's board meetings, subject to the executive-session exception described elsewhere in this document. Civil Code § 4925(a) provides, in relevant part: "Any member may attend board meetings, except when the board adjourns to, or meets solely in, executive session." A related but distinct right lets members speak, not merely attend: Civil Code § 4925(b) provides, "The board shall permit any member to speak at any meeting of the association or the board, except for meetings of the board held in executive session. A reasonable time limit for all members of the association to speak to the board or before a meeting of the association shall be established by the board." These attendance and speaking rights apply to members of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Any member may attend board meetings, except when the board adjourns to, or meets solely in, executive session."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4925(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4925(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4925.)
  "The board shall permit any member to speak at any meeting of the association or the board, except for meetings of the board held in executive session. A reasonable time limit for all members of the association to speak to the board or before a meeting of the association shall be established by the board."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4925(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4925(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4925.)
  Known gap: The citations to § 4925(a) and § 4925(b) are subdivisions of the same statutory section. This clause quotes only the first sentence of § 4925(a); the remainder of that subdivision (not quoted here) separately addresses a member's right to attend, and have audible to them, the open portion of a teleconference board meeting. This clause does not state what a "reasonable" time limit on member speaking is in any specific case -- § 4925(b) leaves that determination to the board itself, subject to the reasonableness standard the statute states. This document does not determine whether any specific time limit or attendance practice of the association's board complies with this standard.

BOARD ACTION GENERALLY LIMITED TO AGENDA ITEMS NOTICED IN ADVANCE
Beyond requiring that action be taken at a meeting at all, California law further restricts a nonemergency meeting to discussing or acting on items that were actually placed on the agenda distributed with the meeting notice. Civil Code § 4930(a) provides: "Except as described in subdivisions (b) to (e), inclusive, the board may not discuss or take action on any item at a nonemergency meeting unless the item was placed on the agenda included in the notice that was distributed pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 4920. This subdivision does not prohibit a member or resident who is not a director from speaking on issues not on the agenda." This agenda-based limit on board discussion and action applies to nonemergency meetings of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association's board.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Except as described in subdivisions (b) to (e), inclusive, the board may not discuss or take action on any item at a nonemergency meeting unless the item was placed on the agenda included in the notice that was distributed pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 4920. This subdivision does not prohibit a member or resident who is not a director from speaking on issues not on the agenda."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4930(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4930(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4930.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a) of § 4930. It does not quote subdivisions (b) through (e) of that same section, which set out specific, narrow exceptions allowing brief staff or director responses to speakers, referrals for information, and -- under defined emergency or supermajority-vote conditions, or where an item carried over from a recent prior meeting -- board action on an item not on the distributed agenda; those exceptions are real and not covered by this clause's single quoted subdivision. This document does not determine whether any specific item discussed or acted on by the association's board was or was not properly on that meeting's noticed agenda, or whether any of the subdivision (b) through (e) exceptions applied to a specific instance.

AVAILABILITY OF MEETING MINUTES AND MEMBERS' RIGHT TO ENFORCE THIS ARTICLE
California law requires that minutes of an open board meeting be made available to members, and separately gives members a civil remedy for violations of these open-meeting requirements. Civil Code § 4950(a) provides, in relevant part: "The minutes, minutes proposed for adoption that are marked to indicate draft status, or a summary of the minutes, of any board meeting, other than an executive session, shall be available to members within 30 days of the meeting." If these requirements are violated, Civil Code § 4955(a) provides: "A member of an association may bring a civil action for declaratory or equitable relief for a violation of this article by the association, including, but not limited to, injunctive relief, restitution, or a combination thereof, within one year of the date the cause of action accrues." Civil Code § 4955(b) adds a fee-shifting and penalty rule: "A member who prevails in a civil action to enforce the member's rights pursuant to this article shall be entitled to reasonable attorney's fees and court costs, and the court may impose a civil penalty of up to five hundred dollars ($500) for each violation, except that each identical violation shall be subject to only one penalty if the violation affects each member equally." These minute-availability and enforcement provisions apply to Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The minutes, minutes proposed for adoption that are marked to indicate draft status, or a summary of the minutes, of any board meeting, other than an executive session, shall be available to members within 30 days of the meeting."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4950(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4950(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4950.)
  "A member of an association may bring a civil action for declaratory or equitable relief for a violation of this article by the association, including, but not limited to, injunctive relief, restitution, or a combination thereof, within one year of the date the cause of action accrues."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4955(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4955(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4955.)
  "A member who prevails in a civil action to enforce the member’s rights pursuant to this article shall be entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and court costs, and the court may impose a civil penalty of up to five hundred dollars ($500) for each violation, except that each identical violation shall be subject to only one penalty if the violation affects each member equally."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4955(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4955(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4955.)
  Known gap: The citation to § 4950(a) is to a section separate from § 4955; § 4950(a) and § 4955(a)-(b) are cited together in this clause because they form a related pair (a recordkeeping/transparency duty and the civil remedy for violating the open-meeting requirements generally, including that duty), not because they are subdivisions of one section -- § 4955(a) and § 4955(b) are, by contrast, subdivisions of the same section as each other. This clause does not quote the remainder of § 4950(a) (the distribution-upon-request-and-reimbursement sentence) or § 4950(b) (the annual policy statement's obligation to inform members how to obtain minutes). This clause does not quote the remainder of § 4955(b) addressing a prevailing association's inability to recover costs absent a frivolousness finding. This document does not determine whether a violation of this article has occurred with respect to the association, whether any specific minutes were timely made available, or whether any member would prevail in, or is well-advised to bring, a civil action under § 4955.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF REVIEW
This information sheet, describing California statutory open-meeting requirements applicable to the board of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association, has been reviewed by the person named below. This acknowledgment confirms only that this information sheet was reviewed; it does not itself constitute board meeting minutes, a notice of meeting, or any other record required by Civil Code §§ 4900-4955, and it does not determine whether any specific meeting, notice, or board action of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association complied with those requirements.

Reviewed by: _________________________ Date: September 4, 2026

Sacramento, California

citations.case: Cal. Civ. Code § 4955(b) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.quote: A member who prevails in a civil action to enforce the member’s rights pursuant to this article shall be entitled to reasonable attorney’s fees and court costs, and the court may impose a civil penalty of up to five hundred dollars ($500) for each violation, except that each identical violation shall be subject to only one penalty if the violation affects each member equally.

expectedJSON.gap: The citation to § 4950(a) is to a section separate from § 4955; § 4950(a) and § 4955(a)-(b) are cited together in this clause because they form a related pair (a recordkeeping/transparency duty and the civil remedy for violating the open-meeting requirements generally, including that duty), not because they are subdivisions of one section -- § 4955(a) and § 4955(b) are, by contrast, subdivisions of the same section as each other. This clause does not quote the remainder of § 4950(a) (the distribution-upon-request-and-reimbursement sentence) or § 4950(b) (the annual policy statement's obligation to inform members how to obtain minutes). This clause does not quote the remainder of § 4955(b) addressing a prevailing association's inability to recover costs absent a frivolousness finding. This document does not determine whether a violation of this article has occurred with respect to the association, whether any specific minutes were timely made available, or whether any member would prevail in, or is well-advised to bring, a civil action under § 4955.

This information sheet, describing California statutory open-meeting requirements applicable to the board of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association, has been reviewed by the person named below. This acknowledgment confirms only that this information sheet was reviewed; it does not itself constitute board meeting minutes, a notice of meeting, or any other record required by Civil Code §§ 4900-4955, and it does not determine whether any specific meeting, notice, or board action of Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association complied with those requirements.
